subtitle: When cannons thundered, Malabar picked up the pen

panels.shot: split-screen wide, stormy sea with distant ships on one side, lamp-lit manuscripts and palm leaves on the other
panels.action: Zainuddin Makhdoom II and Ezhuthachan sit back-to-back, half in shadow, each bent over a manuscript, as beyond them the Malabar coast fades into warships on a churning sea.

dialogue.text: On the Zamorin’s coast, as Portuguese guns growl offshore, Zainuddin Makhdoom II and Ezhuthachan turn Malabar itself into a text of memory and resistance.

i18n.hi: ज़मोरिन के तट पर, दूर पुर्तगाली तोपों की गरज के बीच, ज़ैनुद्दीन मख़दूम द्वितीय और एझुठाचन मलाबार को याद और मुख़ालफ़त की किताब बना देते हैं।

panels.shot: dawn aerial over Calicut, sweeping from crowded harbor to temple spires
panels.action: The sun rises over Calicut’s busy harbor with ships at anchor, then glides inland to reveal the tiled roofs and stone walls of the Tali Shiva temple complex nestled amid coconut palms.

dialogue.text: Calicut in the sixteenth century is not only a merchant city. Behind the smell of pepper and sea salt, its stone courtyards kindle a quieter fire: learning.

i18n.hi: सोलहवीं सदी का कालीकट सिर्फ़ सौदागरों का शहर नहीं। काली मिर्च और समुंदर की गंध के पीछे, पत्थर की चौखटों में एक धीमी आग जलती है — पढ़ाई।

panels.shot: low-angle inside Tali temple hall, scholars seated in rows facing a central dais
panels.action: In the pillared hall of the Tali temple, Brahman scholars sit cross-legged with palm-leaf manuscripts, while a dignified official of the Zamorin stands ready to announce the Revathi Pattathanam contest.

dialogue.text: Each year, under the Revathi star, the Zamorin’s men summon Sanskrit scholars to Tali. The Pattathanam contest turns a temple into an assembly of minds and memory.

i18n.hi: हर साल रेवती नक्षत्र पर, ज़मोरिन के लोग संस्कृत विद्वानों को ताली बुलाते हैं। पत्तथानम मुकाबला मंदिर को दिमाग़ और यादों की सभा बना देता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of an aging scholar reciting, younger scholars listening intently
panels.action: An elderly scholar with ash on his forehead recites verses from a worn manuscript, his hand raised in argument, while younger aspirants lean forward, attentive and tense.

dialogue.text: Logic, grammar, ritual, law—questions flash and answers clash. The prize is not gold alone, but recognition as Pattar, learned in the Vedic, trusted by the Zamorin’s realm.

i18n.hi: तर्क, व्याकरण, कर्मकांड, कानून—सवाल चमकते हैं, जवाब टकराते हैं। इनाम सिर्फ़ सोना नहीं, बल्कि ‘पत्तार’ का मान, वेद-विद्वान जिसे ज़मोरिन का इलाक़ा भरोसा करे।

panels.shot: slow push-in from Tali temple towards coastline, blending into a wide shot of Ponnani mosque
panels.action: The view pulls back from Tali’s inner shrine and sweeps south along the shore, transforming into the sight of Ponnani’s mosque courtyard filled with students and elders around low desks.

dialogue.text: South along the same coast, Ponnani rises as another kind of school. Under the Makhdooms, its mosque courtyards thicken with Arabic texts, Malabari voices and debates of law and faith.

i18n.hi: उसी तट के दक्षिण में, पोनननी एक नई पाठशाला बनकर उठता है। मख़दूमों के साए में मस्जिद के आँगनों में अरबी किताबें, मलाबारी आवाज़ें और कानून-इमान की बहसें गहराती हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Zainuddin as a young scholar among students in Ponnani
panels.action: A younger Zainuddin Makhdoom II sits among students in the mosque portico, an open Arabic manuscript before him as a senior teacher points to a line and explains, while boats glide in the nearby river.

dialogue.text: Zainuddin Makhdoom II grows in this world of study. He learns hadith and law, hears of distant sultans, and watches Portuguese sails creep closer to Malabar’s inlets.

i18n.hi: ज़ैनुद्दीन मख़दूम द्वितीय इसी दुनिया में बड़ा होता है। हदीस और फ़िक़्ह पढ़ता है, दूर के सुल्तानों की बातें सुनता है, और देखता है कि पुर्तगाली जहाज़ मलाबार की खाड़ियाँ नज़दीक तक घुसते जा रहे हैं।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder close-up on Zainuddin’s hand writing Arabic script on paper
panels.action: Zainuddin’s hand moves across a page, inscribing neat Arabic lines, his brow furrowed in concentration, a small oil lamp casting sharp light on the script while the sounds of the harbor drift in.

dialogue.text: By the 1570s and 80s, battles with the Portuguese scar the coast. Zainuddin begins to write not only law, but history: the struggle of Malabar’s Muslims, framed in the language of jihad.

i18n.hi: १५७० और ८० के दशक में पुर्तगालियों से लड़ाइयाँ तट पर घाव छोड़ जाती हैं। ज़ैनुद्दीन अब सिर्फ़ कानून नहीं, इतिहास भी लिखता है—मलाबार के मुसलमानों की जंग, जिसे वह जिहाद की ज़बान में ढालता है।

panels.shot: dramatic side-angle of Zainuddin presenting a bound manuscript to a Deccan envoy
panels.action: In a simple hall, Zainuddin stands and offers a freshly bound manuscript respectfully to a finely dressed envoy from Bijapur, while other scholars watch, the atmosphere solemn.

dialogue.text: He completes Tuhfat al-Mujahidin in 1583, dedicating it to Ali Adil Shah of Bijapur. It is a gift, an exhortation, a chronicle asking Deccan power to answer Malabar’s cry.

i18n.hi: वह १५८३ में ‘तुहफ़तुल-मुजाहिदीन’ पूरा करता है, इसे बीजापुर के अली आदिल शाह के नाम करता है। यह तोहफ़ा भी है, पुकार भी, दकन की ताक़त से मलाबार की चीख़ का जवाब माँगती दास्तान भी।

panels.shot: close-up on Zainuddin’s thoughtful face, shadowed, with a faint view of ships in the distance
panels.action: Zainuddin looks out from Ponnani’s shore toward distant masts on the horizon, his face set, the manuscript rolls beside him, waves breaking at his feet.

dialogue.text: If we forget these years, our children will forget their duty.

i18n.hi: अगर हम इन सालों को भूल गए, तो हमारे बच्चे अपना फ़र्ज़ भूल जाएँगे।

panels.shot: wide shot of a teacher reading from Tuhfat to a circle of Mappila listeners
panels.action: Under a shady tree near the mosque, a teacher reads from Tuhfat al-Mujahidin aloud to fishermen, traders, and young students seated around him, the book resting on a wooden stand.

dialogue.text: Tuhfat is no neutral chronicle. It names the Portuguese as oppressors, recalls battles, praises martyrs, and urges Malabar’s Muslims and their allies toward armed struggle and steadfast faith.

i18n.hi: ‘तुहफ़त’ कोई ठंडी तारीख़ नहीं। यह पुर्तगालियों को ज़ालिम कहकर पुकारती है, लड़ाइयाँ याद करती है, शहीदों की तारीफ़ करती है, और मलाबार के मुसलमानों व उनके साथियों को हथियारबंद जंग और मज़बूत ईमान की तरफ बुलाती है।

panels.shot: crossfade-style composition: temple scholars on the left, mosque scholars on the right, separated by a thin strip of shoreline
panels.action: On one side, Tali’s Sanskrit scholars gesture over palm leaves; on the other, Ponnani’s ulama discourse over Arabic texts, with a bright strip of sand and sea dividing yet linking the scenes.

dialogue.text: Two intellectual worlds share the same monsoon winds. Sanskrit at Tali, Arabic-Malayalam at Ponnani—overlapping in geography, distinct in lineage and aims.

i18n.hi: दो इल्मी दुनिया एक ही मानसून की हवा बाँटती हैं। ताली में संस्कृत, पोनननी में अरबी–मलयालम—ज़मीन पर साथ, नसब और मक़सद में अलग।

panels.shot: evening interior of a modest house in Tirur or nearby, Ezhuthachan seated with palm-leaf and stylus
panels.action: In a humble, lamplit room with a simple mat and wooden beam ceiling, Ezhuthachan sits cross-legged, stylus poised over a palm leaf, as a mynah bird perches nearby.

dialogue.text: Elsewhere along Malabar, another quiet figure shapes its language. Ezhuthachan’s dates are debated, but his voice enters the sixteenth-century air through devotional retellings in Malayalam.

i18n.hi: मलाबार के किसी और मोड़ पर, एक चुप-सा आदमी इसकी भाषा को गढ़ता है। एझुठाचन की तारीख़ें लड़खड़ाती हैं, मगर उसकी आवाज़ सोलहवीं सदी में मलयालम की भक्तिमय कहानियों से उतरती है।

panels.shot: gentle close-up on Ezhuthachan reciting to a small group in kilippattu style
panels.action: Ezhuthachan recites lines in a soft, steady tone to villagers and children seated before him, while a bird, the imagined kili, sits on a stand, anchoring the kilippattu storytelling mood.

dialogue.text: In Adhyatma Ramayanam and Mahabharatam kilippattu traditions, the parrot’s voice leads listeners into epic tales. The stories are old; the Malayalam cadence, newly made wide and intimate.

i18n.hi: ‘आध्यात्म रामायणम्’ और ‘महाभरतम् किलिप्पट्टु’ में तोते की आवाज़ श्रोताओं को महाकाव्यों में ले जाती है। किस्से पुराने हैं; मलयालम की लय नई, चौड़ी और दिल के क़रीब।

panels.shot: overhead shot of Ezhuthachan’s hand writing Malayalam in the evolving script on palm leaf
panels.action: Ezhuthachan’s hand steadily inscribes Malayalam verses onto palm leaves using the rounded script, a small pile of completed leaves beside him and a quiet sense of methodical work.

dialogue.text: Scholars debate the exact dates and details of his life. What stands clear is his role in shaping literary Malayalam, making Sanskritic devotion accessible to everyday speakers of the tongue.

i18n.hi: विद्वान उसके जीवन की सही तारीख़ों और बातों पर बहस करते रहते हैं। जो साफ़ दिखता है, वह है साहित्यिक मलयालम को गढ़ने में उसका हाथ—संस्कृत-भक्ति को रोज़ बोलने वालों की ज़बान तक लाना।

panels.shot: medium shot of common townsfolk listening, some with hands folded, to a reading of Adhyatma Ramayanam
panels.action: In a village courtyard, men and women of varied ages sit in a circle at dusk, listening with folded hands as a reader chants from Adhyatma Ramayanam, palm leaves laid out before him.

dialogue.text: Now you can hear Rama’s journey in your own words.

i18n.hi: अब राम की यात्रा तुम अपनी भाषा में सुन सकते हो।

panels.shot: symbolic wide shot: sea with warships faintly visible, inland scenes of reading Tuhfat and kilippattu side by side
panels.action: In one half, Mappila youths listen as Tuhfat is read near Ponnani’s shore; in the other, villagers gather for kilippattu recitation; in the distance, faint silhouettes of Portuguese caravels sit on the water.

dialogue.text: While cannon smoke hangs over the sea, Malabar’s coast hums with words. Some texts call for armed resistance; others call hearts inward through devotion. All work on memory.

i18n.hi: जब समुंदर पर तोपों का धुआँ तना है, मलाबार का तट शब्दों से गूँज रहा है। कुछ किताबें हथियारबंद मुख़ालफ़त बुलाती हैं; कुछ दिलों को भीतर की भक्ति में मोड़ती हैं। सब याद पर काम कर रही हैं।

panels.shot: library-like montage of manuscripts: Tuhfat, Sanskrit palm leaves, Malayalam kilippattu, stacked together
panels.action: A still composition of different manuscripts—Arabic-script Tuhfat, palm-leaf Sanskrit texts from Tali, Malayalam verse leaves associated with Ezhuthachan—resting together on a wooden table.

dialogue.text: Later ages will catalogue and argue: which year, which patron, which text first. Yet the sixteenth century’s coastline already holds a multilingual archive of how Malabar saw itself.

i18n.hi: आने वाली सदियाँ गिनेंगी और बहस करेंगी—कौन साल, कौन सरपरस्त, कौन किताब पहले। पर सोलहवीं सदी का यह तट पहले ही मलाबार की खुद की तस्वीरों का बहुभाषी ख़ज़ाना सँभाले बैठा है।

panels.shot: modern-day low-angle of Tali temple gopuram and Ponnani mosque minaret in the distance, under the same sky
panels.action: Under a single expanse of sky, the Tali temple’s gopuram rises in one direction and the minaret of Ponnani mosque in another, with modern houses and trees between them.

dialogue.text: Today, the stones of Tali and Ponnani stand quiet. Their old contests and classes remind us that Malabar’s battles were fought with ships and steel, but also with stories and chronicles.

i18n.hi: आज ताली और पोनननी के पत्थर शांत खड़े हैं। वहाँ की पुरानी बहसें और क्लास याद दिलाती हैं कि मलाबार की लड़ाइयाँ जहाज़ और इस्पात से ही नहीं, कहानियों और तवारीख़ से भी लड़ी गईं।

panels.shot: final contemplative shot of Zainuddin and Ezhuthachan as statues or imagined figures, surrounded by floating verses
panels.action: Idealized figures of Zainuddin and Ezhuthachan sit facing opposite directions, eyes lowered in thought, as faint lines of Arabic and Malayalam script swirl around them like mist.

dialogue.text: In their different tongues, Zainuddin and Ezhuthachan show a coast under siege choosing to remember itself. A culture is defended by memory as much as by arms, and its strongest citadel is the word.

i18n.hi: अपनी अलग-अलग ज़बानों में, ज़ैनुद्दीन और एझुठाचन दिखाते हैं कि घिरे हुए इस तट ने खुद को याद रखना चुना। एक तहज़ीब याद से उतनी ही बचती है जितनी हथियार से, और इसका सबसे मज़बूत क़िला होता है शब्द।

title_i18n.hi: ताली के विद्वान, मलयालम की आवाज़ें

subtitle_i18n.en: When cannons thundered, Malabar picked up the pen
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब तोपें गरजीं, मलाबार ने कलम उठा ली
